html:
At the River Boyne, on 1 July 1690 (11 July in today's calendar), the Protestant King William III defeated the Catholic King James II, whom he had replaced on the English throne.

James had fled England in the Glorious Revolution of 1688 and came to Ireland with French help to win back his crowns. Irish Catholics backed him; the Protestants of the north backed William, whose army included Dutch, Danish and Huguenot troops. James lost and fled to France. The war in Ireland ended with the Treaty of Limerick in 1691.

The victory began the Protestant Ascendancy: the penal laws shut Catholics out of land, office and the professions for a century. Protestants in Northern Ireland still celebrate the battle with Orange marches each 12 July. See Ireland, Ulster and the Troubles.
sum: At the River Boyne, on 1 July 1690 (11 July in today's calendar), the Protestant King William III defeated the Catholic King James II, whom he had replaced on the English throne.
